description: Turn Activity and Coder Session into scannable execution-evidence views with attention-first event classification, stable session evidence regions, project-scoped navigation, and shared light/dark status treatment, consuming recorded events via a project-scoped read endpoint plus existing snapshots.

tasks.title: Add project-scoped event read endpoint for Activity evidence
tasks.description: Add a server-side project-scoped event read endpoint (GET /api/projects/:projectRef/events) that queries existing recorded events across issues, workflow runs, and agent sessions within a project, sorted by time. This reads already-stored events without changing how they are recorded and without adding event subscription behavior, resolving the project-scoped recorded-event prerequisite for T-002.
acceptanceCriteria: The endpoint GET /api/projects/:projectRef/events returns a time-sorted list of recorded events across issues, workflow runs, and agent sessions within the specified project.

Each event includes enough context (event type, source aggregate type, issue number, workflow run id, session id, runner id where applicable) for the Web projection to classify it as issue-state, workflow-stage, agent-session, runner, or failure evidence.
The endpoint queries existing stored events from the per-aggregate event tables without changing how events are recorded, emitted, or subscribed.
The endpoint supports a limit parameter with a sensible default and returns events most-recent-first.
Server spec tests verify cross-aggregate event retrieval, time ordering, project scoping, and that no event recording or subscription behavior is added.
npm test (server) passes.
tasks.output: Project-scoped event read endpoint in packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/ with a new querier or IEventStore method, plus server spec tests
tasks.notes: Resolves the project-scoped recorded-event prerequisite for T-002. Does not change event recording or add subscription behavior. Events are already stored per-aggregate in IssueEvents, WorkflowRunEvents, EpicEvents, and AgentSessionEvents tables; the endpoint queries across them by project. The existing per-issue endpoint GET /api/projects/:projectRef/issues/:number/events and WorkflowEventQuerier.ListIssueEventsAsync are reference points for the DTO shape.

tasks.title: Reorganize Coder Session into a structured execution-evidence view
tasks.description: Formalize the existing Coder Session shell into stable regions for task identity and status, usage, errors, transcript turns and tool calls, follow-up actions, and sibling evidence. Add the read-only errors summary, workflow-context navigation, Activity return orientation, and reliable resolution of the existing issue-session ID route while preserving existing transcript, cancel, recovery, follow-up, sibling, and lineage behavior, and migrate all session status surfaces to the shared theme-token families.
acceptanceCriteria: SessionDetailShell renders recognizable, stable regions for task identity/current status, optional usage, optional errors, transcript turns and tool calls, follow-up actions, and optional sibling sessions; sessions without usage, errors, turns, or siblings degrade without moving or merging the remaining regions.

A compact session-errors-region appears above the transcript when statusKind is failed, failureCategory is present, or toolErrorCount is greater than zero; it renders failureReason only when available, exposes data-failure-category and data-tool-error-count for verification, and is absent when no error evidence exists.

The existing transcript hierarchy continues to distinguish tool calls from message turns, and the transcript scroll container, sticky title, sticky recovery bar, follow-up composer, sibling navigation slot, lineage link, and cancel confirmation anchors and behavior remain available with their existing gating semantics.

Issue-bound sessions expose project-scoped entry points to the relevant issue and workflow context; the existing /issues/:number/session/:sessionId route resolves the session ID to the canonical session name before detail queries; Activity-origin links return to the project-scoped Activity page; sibling and lineage links remain project-scoped; generic sessions without an issue link to their agent context and do not fabricate issue or workflow links.

Status badges for running, completed, failed, stale, probing, and finalizing sessions, plus failure, recovery, context-health, usage, follow-up, sibling, and transcript tool success/failure accents, use the shared success/warning/info/danger and neutral surface token families in light and dark mode; no parallel shared status helper or hardcoded semantic red/amber/yellow/blue/green palette remains on these session status surfaces.

The implementation consumes the existing session metadata, transcript, usage, sibling, and lineage data sources without API, DTO, query, transcript-recording, subscription, or action-semantics changes and without exposing raw implementation field names as labels.

Existing SessionPage sticky, cancel, lineage, follow-up, GenericSessionPage, and tests/SessionPageHeader.spec.tsx coverage are updated and pass; focused spec coverage verifies region order and optional-region degradation, error presence/absence, issue-session ID resolution, Activity return orientation, project-scoped navigation, action preservation, and shared token classes in both themes using existing DI seams and MSW without vi.mock.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: Structured Coder Session evidence layout in packages/web/src/pages/session and related coder-session/session-health/session-transcript widgets, with preserved actions, direct-link resolution, return orientation, and updated unit/spec tests
tasks.notes: Covers the complete coder-session-evidence-view capability and design D4-D7. Keep session-recovery-bar inside the transcript scroll container, make session-errors-region read-only, preserve existing test anchors where still valid, and use local inline status-presentation records rather than reintroducing shared/status-presentation. T-002 depends on this task's issue-session ID resolution and from=activity back-target handling.

tasks.title: Replace Activity session cards with an attention-first event evidence feed
tasks.description: Build a pure ActivityEvent projection over the project-scoped event read endpoint (T-000) plus the existing activity and runner snapshots, then replace the Active/Waiting/Recent card sections with event entries carrying production event type, attention level, timestamps, and navigation targets. Deliver the collapsible attention and routine zones, event/attention filters, generic-session coverage, direct evidence links, and shared theme-token treatment as one usable Activity module.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure buildActivityEvents projection and composing hook produce ActivityEvent entries with type, attention, time, domain-language title/description, and project-scoped targets from recorded events plus current snapshots; entries distinguish issue-state, workflow-stage, agent-session, runner, and failure evidence without relabeling current-state snapshots as unavailable transitions.

Recorded failed lifecycle events produce failure attention while retaining their separate recorded agent-session lifecycle evidence; current inactive session snapshots do not fabricate completed, cancelled, or failed transitions; waiting rows produce approval attention; stale/offline runner rows produce blocked attention while busy runners produce routine runner evidence and idle runners remain summarized; all entries have deterministic ordering and duplicate evidence is merged only once.

Generic agent-launched and workflow-bound sessions already present in the activity feed appear together with the same agent-session event identity; workflow sessions link directly through /issues/:number/session/:sessionId with from=activity, generic sessions link directly through /agent-sessions/:sessionId with from=activity, and generic sessions use agentId/agentName without fabricated issue context or duplicate fetching.

ActivityPage renders activity-attention-zone before activity-routine-zone whenever failure, approval, or blocked entries exist, omits the attention zone entirely when none exist, and orders entries most-recent-first within their attention/type grouping so routine evidence never precedes needs-attention evidence on the first screen.

The activity-filter-bar can isolate each supported event type and attention-only evidence and can clear filters to restore the complete attention-ordered feed; every activity-event-entry exposes data-event-type and data-attention identities.

Every applicable entry provides the most specific project-scoped primary destination plus available issue, workflow-context, session, agent, or runner secondary targets; session destinations preserve a project-scoped Activity back target, activity-runners-link remains available, and no context-less root route is introduced.

Activity event entries, attention markers, filters, StatusBar/runner/session status surfaces, and issue-event-timeline category and marker styles use shared success/warning/info/danger and neutral surface token families in light and dark mode; hardcoded semantic red/amber/orange/yellow/blue/green/gray palette classes covered by design D5 are removed without adding a shared status-presentation module.

The feature consumes the project-scoped event read endpoint (T-000) for recorded transitions plus the existing activity, session, and runner snapshots; it adds no event-recording, event-emission, transcript-recording, or event/session-subscription behavior and exposes only production/domain labels.

Collocated activity-events unit tests cover recorded-event and snapshot classification, refusal to fabricate terminal transitions, ordering, generic-session identity/deduplication, and target construction; ActivityPage and new evidence-view spec tests cover event identity, attention-zone presence/absence and prominence, filtering/clearing, direct navigation and return orientation, and light/dark token classes using MSW/DI seams and fake timers without vi.mock or wall-clock waits.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: ActivityEvent projection and attention-first ActivityPage feed in packages/web/src/pages/activity and related activity/session/timeline/runner widgets, with complete unit/spec coverage
tasks.notes: Covers the complete activity-evidence-view capability and design D1-D3 plus D5-D7. Do not reuse EventTimelinePanel, infer transitions from snapshots, or add subscription behavior. The project-scoped recorded-event read endpoint is delivered by T-000. Preserve activity-runners-link, route all links through useProjectPath(), consume T-001's issue-session ID resolution and from=activity handling, control Activity timers in tests, and keep filter-chip logic local rather than extracting a speculative shared component.
